apa: Lu, Y.-C., & Romps, D. M. (2022). Extending the Heat Index. Journal of Applied Meteorology and Climatology, 61(10), 1367-1383. https://doi.org/10.1175/JAMC-D-22-0021.1
how: Read the front page of the eScholarship PDF copy (https://escholarship.org/uc/item/5qw5f679): title, authors, journal 61(10), 2022-10-01, DOI. Read the introduction: the Heat Index uses Steadman's model; polynomial fits (Rothfusz 1990) are used by the National Weather Service.
used_for: Background: what the heat index is and that the National Weather Service uses a polynomial fit.

apa: Widjaja, M., Halim, D. K., & Andarini, R. (2022). The development of an IoT-based indoor air monitoring system towards smart energy efficient classroom. Ultima Computing: Jurnal Sistem Komputer, 14(1), 28-35. https://doi.org/10.31937/sk.v14i1.2565
how: Read the article page on ejournals.umn.ac.id (published 2022-07-17) and the Garuda record: title, authors, volume, pages, DOI. The abstract says indoor air temperature and relative humidity are two essential components of thermal comfort.
used_for: Related work: an IoT classroom temperature and humidity logger with a DHT22 and ESP8266/ESP32.

apa: Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration. (2024, April 12). Official statement on creating extreme heat protocol [Press release]. DOST-PAGASA. https://www.pagasa.dost.gov.ph/index.php/press-release/155
how: Read the page: dated 12 April 2024, signed by the PAGASA Administrator. It says a 4-tier effect-based classification is used and that school heads and local governments should have the final say on decisions.
used_for: Official source that PAGASA uses a four-tier, effect-based heat index classification and leaves school decisions to school heads and local governments. The tier ranges (27-32, 33-41, 42-51, 52 and above) are NOT in this source; they are project decision D-019 and need a PAGASA table before the paper cites a source for them.

apa: Petaca, M. A. (2026, April 22). Heat index monitoring and early warning system of DOST-PAGASA [Slide presentation]. DOST-PAGASA, Climatology and Agrometeorology Division. https://pubfiles.pagasa.dost.gov.ph/climps/climateforum/special_lecture.pdf
how: Downloaded the PDF (14 slides) and looked at every slide as an image. Slide 1: title, author (Weather Specialist, IAAS-CAD, DOST-PAGASA), date 22 April 2026. Slide 4 (effect-based classification): Caution 27-32 C, Extreme Caution 33-41 C, Danger 42-51 C, Extreme Danger 52 C and beyond, each with its effect on the body.
used_for: Source of the four PAGASA tier ranges used by the app (D-019) and of their effects on the body. It is a conference-style slide deck from PAGASA, not a peer-reviewed article; the paper says so.

apa: Tzintzun, I., Schwarz, L., Lawrence, A., & Thomas, M. (2026). Effects of extreme temperature exposure on learning (ADB Economics Working Paper Series No. 866). Asian Development Bank. https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/publication/1185876/ewp-866-extreme-temperature-exposure-learning.pdf
how: Downloaded the PDF and read its first pages with a PDF reader: title, four authors, series number 866, October 2026, abstract (730,000 Cambodian students, sustained heat exposure significantly reduces performance).
used_for: Rationale: heat exposure lowers learning outcomes in a Southeast Asian country. It is a working paper (research in progress), not a peer-reviewed article; the paper says so.

apa: Kirkil, G. (2025). Effects of classroom temperature and humidity on student learning performance: an experimental study using sensor-based monitoring. Frontiers in Built Environment, 11, Article 1678438. https://doi.org/10.3389/fbuil.2025.1678438
how: Opened the full-text page on frontiersin.org (https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/built-environment/articles/10.3389/fbuil.2025.1678438/full) and read the abstract and the start of the article; DOI registry metadata matches (author, title, volume 11, article 1678438, 19 December 2025). Abstract: 2-week experiment, 53 undergraduate students, 20 and 27 C, Arduino-based temperature and humidity sensors, thermal satisfaction and GPA account for 23.15 % of the variance in grades (p < 0.001); limits: no mean radiant temperature, short duration.
used_for: Rationale: classroom thermal conditions and learning outcomes, measured with Arduino sensors. The paper says it was a short university study in Turkiye, so it does not prove the effect for Philippine classrooms.

apa: Wardani, I. K., Ichniarsyah, A. N., Telaumbanua, M., Priyonggo, B., Fil’aini, R., Mufidah, Z., & Dewangga, D. A. (2023). The feasibility study: Accuracy and precision of DHT 22 in measuring the temperature and humidity in the greenhouse. IOP Conference Series: Earth and Environmental Science, 1230(1), Article 012146. https://doi.org/10.1088/1755-1315/1230/1/012146
how: Opened the article page on iopscience.iop.org and read the abstract, authors, volume and conference (FSSAT 4, 15-16 February 2023); DOI registry metadata matches (published 2023-09-01). Abstract: three DHT22 sensors with an ESP32 sending to Ubidots, compared with a thermo-hygrometer; RMSE 1.48 C and 3.18 %, correlations 0.81 and 0.85. The PDF itself was blocked to my script, so only the article page and abstract were read.
used_for: Limitation: a DHT22 with an ESP32 had errors larger than the datasheet figures against a reference instrument, so the accuracy check in this study's recommendations matters. A conference paper from a greenhouse setting, not a classroom.
